APT-ENG-0101: The error lies in segment (D) 'when she started jumping'. The correlative conjunction pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. The standard pattern is 'No sooner did + subject + V1 ... than + clause'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did Priya get her report card than she started jumping with joy.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0102: The error lies in part (2) 'he finally decided to call off from'. The phrasal verb 'call off' means to cancel an event and does not take the preposition 'from'. The intended expression for withdrawing from or abandoning an enterprise is 'pull out of' or 'walk away from'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0103: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'Father took the newspaper in his hand to go through it once again' is idiomatic, grammatically sound, and follows correct prepositional and infinitive usage. Hence, option A ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0104: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. The past time indicator 'a week ago' correctly pairs with the simple past verb 'received'. Hence, option B ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0105: The error lies in segment (A) 'badly to need'. The idiomatic prepositional phrase expressing urgent requirement is 'in bad need of' or 'badly in need of', not 'to need'. Correct sentence: 'This hall is badly in need of repair.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0106: The error lies in segment (B) 'but he had got'. The adverb 'now' indicates a current, present state, requiring the present perfect tense ('has got' or 'has found') rather than the past perfect tense ('had got'). Correct sentence: 'My brother lost his job during the lockdown, but he has got a new job now.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0107: The error lies in segment (B) 'since two hours'. The time expression 'two hours' denotes a duration or period of time, which requires the preposition 'for' rather than 'since' (which denotes a starting point in time). Correct sentence: 'As it has been raining heavily for two hours, the children are at home.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0108: The error lies in segment (D) 'we will have'. This is an inverted third conditional sentence ('Had you not reached in time...'), which requires 'would have + past participle' in the main clause, not 'will have'. Correct sentence: 'Had you not reached in time, we would have lost our lives.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0109: The error lies in segment (B) 'to chase out'. The phrasal verb meaning to track down or pursue debtors to recover unpaid funds is 'chase down' or 'chase up'. 'Chase out' means to drive away physically. Correct sentence: 'It is his job to chase down clients with outstanding debts.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0110: The error lies in segment (D) 'extremely good'. The verb 'performed' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('well'), not the adjective 'good'. Correct sentence: 'My brother performed extremely well in the class test held yesterday.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0111: The error lies in segment (A) 'they were governed'. The main clause establishes a current general fact ('Nowadays, common people take interest...'). The relative clause must therefore be in the present tense ('they are governed'), not the past tense ('they were governed'). Correct sentence: 'Nowadays, common people take interest in the manner in which they are governed.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0112: The error lies in segment (C) 'giving in the prizes'. The correct phrasal verb meaning to distribute prizes or gifts freely is 'give away' (here: 'giving away'). 'Give in' means to surrender or yield. Correct sentence: 'The companies were giving away the prizes to attract customers during the festive season.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0113: The error lies in segment (D) 'We has travelled'. The first-person plural subject pronoun 'We' takes the plural auxiliary verb 'have', not the singular 'has'. Correct sentence: 'We have travelled to many states of India to get an essence of its diversity.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0114: The error lies in segment (3) 'and ran over'. The phrasal verb 'run over' means to hit or knock down with a vehicle. The intended phrasal verb meaning to meet someone unexpectedly is 'run into' or 'run across'. Correct sentence: 'Ganga was out shopping at the mall and ran into her schoolmate.' Since segment 3 corresponds to option A, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0115: The error lies in segment (2) 'grew out'. The standard phrasal verb meaning to develop and mature from childhood into adulthood is 'grow up' (past tense 'grew up'). 'Grow out' means to become too large for clothes. Correct sentence: 'When Christy grew up, he turned out to be a gentleman.' Since segment 2 corresponds to option D, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0116: The error lies in segment (C) 'in every Tuesday'. Time adverbials containing determiners like 'every', 'each', 'this', or 'next' do not take a preposition ('in', 'on', 'at'). It should be simply 'every Tuesday'. Correct sentence: 'Going to the weekly market every Tuesday is a ritual that has been followed by generations in my family.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0117: The error lies in segment (B) 'did not went to'. Following the auxiliary 'did / did not', the main verb must appear in its base form (bare infinitive V1 'go'), not the past tense 'went'. Correct sentence: 'I noticed that they did not go to the museum but entered a shopping complex.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0118: The error lies in segment (B) 'that he truthful'. The verb 'answered' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('truthfully'), not an adjective ('truthful'). Correct sentence: 'It was noticed that he truthfully answered the questions raised by the Headmistress.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0119: The error lies in segment (C) 'fastly above'. 'Fast' serves as both an adjective and an adverb in English; 'fastly' is non-standard and grammatically incorrect. Correct sentence: 'The birds flew fast above as we stood on our terrace.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0120: The error lies in segment (C) 'among you is to baked the'. After the infinitive marker 'to', the verb must take its base form (V1 'bake'), not the past participle form 'baked'. Correct sentence: '...“Who among you is to bake the Christmas cake this year?”' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0121: The error lies in segment (C) 'if you will'. In conditional sentences (first conditional), the subordinate clause introduced by 'if' takes the simple present tense ('if you ask her'), not the modal auxiliary 'will'. Correct sentence: 'The teacher will certainly help you if you ask her.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0122: The error lies in segment (C) 'if you will'. In a conditional clause denoting a future contingency ('if'-clause), the simple present tense is used instead of the future tense with 'will'. Correct sentence: 'The teacher will never give you punishment if you come on time.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0123: The error lies in segment (C) 'he travels by foot'. The standard idiomatic prepositional phrase for walking is 'on foot', not 'by foot'. Correct sentence: 'Whenever he is on a holiday, he travels on foot to the temple nearby.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0124: The error lies in segment (C) 'A great'. The noun phrase 'culture of hospitality of the Spanish' refers to a specific, uniquely identified cultural attribute and therefore requires the definite article 'The' rather than the indefinite article 'A'. Correct sentence: 'The great culture of hospitality of the Spanish is well-known.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0125: The error lies in segment (D) 'that he will praying'. The modal auxiliary 'will' cannot be directly followed by a present participle ('praying'). It requires either the simple future ('will pray') or the continuous aspect auxiliary ('will be praying'). Correct sentence: 'I am sure that he will pray for a good crop this year.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0126: The error lies in segment (A) 'in an east'. Cardinal directions (east, west, north, south) refer to unique geographical entities and take the definite article 'the', not 'an'. Correct sentence: 'The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0127: The error lies in segment (D) 'show on'. The phrasal verb meaning to display one's possessions or abilities ostentatiously is 'show off', not 'show on'. Correct sentence: 'She always likes to show off her wealth.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0128: The error lies in segment (A) 'the very well-directed film'. When mentioning a single countable entity for the first time in an indefinite context, the indefinite article 'a' is required ('a very well-directed film'). Correct sentence: 'It was a very well-directed film and we enjoyed it.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0129: The error lies in the underlined word 'go' (option A). When two sequential actions in the past are described, the earlier action takes the past perfect ('had gone') and the subsequent action takes the simple past ('went'), not the present tense 'go'. Correct sentence: 'I had gone to Siliguri before I went to Raiganj.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0130: The error lies in segment (D) 'to an range of health problems'. The word 'range' begins with a consonant sound (/r/), requiring the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an'. Correct sentence: '...to a range of health problems in both children and adults.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0131: The error lies in segment (B) 'how the thieves enter'. The sentence narrates completed past events ('reported', 'was a mystery'). The break-in must therefore be expressed in the past tense ('entered' or 'had entered') rather than the present tense 'enter'. Correct sentence: 'The newspaper reported that it was a mystery how the thieves entered the house.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0132: The error lies in segment (C) 'to meet society new needs'. The noun 'society' functions possessively with respect to 'needs' and requires the possessive inflection 'society's'. Correct sentence: 'Workers and companies in all sectors can contribute their skills to meet society's new needs.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0133: The error lies in segment (D) 'in a'. The word 'hour' begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound (/aʊər/), requiring the indefinite article 'an' rather than 'a'. Correct sentence: 'He will return in an hour.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0134: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. The spelling of 'stationery' (writing materials) is correct, the subject-verb agreement ('there is a delay') is sound, and the causal phrase 'due to the faulty purchase orders' is appropriate. Hence, option D ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0135: The error lies in segment (B) 'It is imperative in understanding'. The adjective 'imperative' takes an infinitive complement ('imperative to understand') or a subordinate clause ('imperative that...'), not a prepositional gerund phrase ('in understanding'). Correct sentence: 'It is imperative to understand the rising importance of artificial intelligence...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0136: The error lies in segment (C) 'After knowing truth'. The noun 'truth' when referring to the facts of a specific case requires the definite article 'the' ('the truth'). Correct sentence: 'After knowing the truth, the jury took the right decision in the case.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0137: The error lies in segment (A) 'A honourable person'. The word 'honourable' begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound (/ɒ/), requiring the indefinite article 'An' instead of 'A'. Segment (A) corresponds to option D. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0138: The error lies in segment (C) 'that Ben will done'. The modal auxiliary 'will' must be followed by a base form verb (V1 'do') or 'have done' in the future perfect. In indirect speech after the past reporting verb 'said', it should be 'would do'. Correct sentence: 'My mother said that Ben would do the assignment today.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0139: The error lies in the underlined portion in option D: 'had it store'. The idiomatic expression meaning destined or prepared for someone in the future is 'in store' ('had in store for them'), not 'had it store'. Correct phrase: 'what fate had in store for them'. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0140: The error lies in segment (D) 'Vijay and Ajay is here'. The compound subject 'Vijay and Ajay' consists of two entities joined by 'and', which takes the plural verb 'are', not 'is'. Correct sentence: 'Vijay and Ajay are here to celebrate 7 years of their friendship.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0141: The error lies in segment (D) 'but it still deny'. The subject pronoun 'it' is third-person singular and takes the singular verb 'denies' in the simple present tense, not the base form 'deny'. Correct sentence: 'The company was sued for breach of contract, but it still denies any wrongdoing.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0142: The error lies in segment (D) 'to plan our course careful'. The verb 'plan' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('carefully'), not an adjective ('careful'). Correct sentence: 'In this world of competitions, every one of us is required to plan our course carefully.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0143: The error lies in option D 'itinary'. The word is misspelled; the correct English spelling is 'itinerary' (a planned route or journey). Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0144: The error lies in option B 'colleages'. The word is misspelled; the correct English spelling is 'colleagues' (coworkers/fellow associates). Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0145: The error lies in the underlined word 'being' (option C). In the present perfect continuous tense ('has not been + V-ing'), the auxiliary verb must be 'been', not 'being'. Correct sentence: 'The Dutta company has not been making new school bags since the lockdown commenced.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0146: The error lies in segment (A) 'French'. When referring to the entire people or nation of France, the definite article 'the' is required ('the French'), matching 'The English'. Correct sentence: 'The English often fought the French.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0147: The error lies in segment (A) 'the thieves have leave'. The auxiliary 'have' requires the past participle form 'left' ('have left'), and in the past sequence following 'recalled', the past perfect 'had left' is required. Correct sentence: 'He finally recalled that the thieves had left from the front door.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
